method: Independent clean-room read-only supplemental review of the current frozen source. Read AGENTS.md and followed the user's two-clean-round gate override; no full suite. Initial inventory scope was verified as exactly 69 web/tests paths, correcting the initial numeric count; parent then narrowed this review to the exact 25 paths in .work/r13-web-test-assignment-a.json. All 25 assigned files were read completely, including every test/fixture body, assertion, mock route, deferred-promise control, lifecycle cleanup, fake-timer path, security/ownership condition and malformed-input case. Read 12 additional complete web test files before/alongside routing and 12 complete supporting source/configuration files, for 49 actually inspected inventory paths. No AST-only coverage claim, previous checkout, Git history or previous audit findings/reports were used. Cross-referenced the actual Api, event/session/resource/watch hooks and message media implementation. Before inspection of test bodies, independently recomputed all 1901 raw file SHA-256 values with zero mismatches and invoked the pinned Node runtime's current scripts/snapshot.mjs; aggregate digest and count matched the frozen inventory. Repeated all 1901 raw hashes and canonical snapshot digest at completion, again with zero mismatches and unchanged digest. A concrete partial-failure polling concern justified one isolated mocked-API, fake-clock hook reproduction under .work: final .work/r13-watch-overlap.test.tsx ran alone using .work/r13-watch-overlap.vitest.ts and pinned Node 24.22.1, passed one assertion-based reproduction with zero skips, and recorded starts/signals in .work/r13-watch-overlap-observation.json and the Vitest result in .work/r13-watch-overlap-result.json. The mock deliberately leaves sibling reads pending and does not implement Api.call's 30000 ms timeout; the observation establishes overlap within 5000 ms, not unbounded production requests. Three preliminary reproduction harness attempts timed out because the ad-hoc harness recreated the mock API object each render; corrected stable-API reproduction passed and only that final observation supports the finding. No production/source edits, external network requests, live credentials, model calls, remote operations or full-suite tests.

findings.title: Wait for all workspace-watch reads before scheduling the next poll
findings.evidence: read() awaits Promise.all at lines 32-54, which rejects as soon as one path fails. Its finally block at lines 69-70 schedules another read after 5000 ms without waiting for or canceling the other path. The isolated final reproduction makes directory metadata fail while file.txt metadata remains pending: starts at 1793210897176 and 1793210902176 show a second file.txt read exactly 5000 ms later, with two unresolved file reads and signalsAbortedBeforeUnmount=[false,false]. The complete existing web/tests/workspace-watch.test.tsx covers all-pending reads and successful/deleted snapshots, but not a failed sibling with another read pending. Api.call in web/lib/api.ts gives workspace/metadata a 30000 ms timeout, so timeout bounds each actual request lifetime but does not prevent this demonstrated overlap.
findings.impact: When either monitored path repeatedly fails quickly and the other is slow, the browser starts duplicate metadata work every five seconds while earlier work is still pending, increasing load precisely during an error condition and violating the watcher's non-overlapping poll contract. Wait for all started path reads to settle, or cancel and settle the surviving reads, before scheduling the next poll; add the failed-sibling/pending-read regression case. This finding does not claim unbounded request lifetime or observed production data loss.
